summary: universal_address_writer_equivariance covers four modeled address-bearing entrypoint projections. Only requestWithdrawals and unwrap have the proved pause/balance/allowance permissionless-admission lemma; transferFrom and claimWithdrawalsTo retain caller-relative owner/approval gates. The separate AddressClaimBatchTx executes arbitrary-length parallel request/hint iteration and has a bounded two-item observe receipt for packed request/checkpoint reads, claimed-bit writes, locked-ETH decrements, and ordered value-bearing payout CALLs. It is incremental transaction evidence, not a widening of the universal parent.

theorems.name: LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PAddress1.universal_address_writer_equivariance
theorems.doc:
/-- Two nonzero callers have the same source-shaped admission bit, and a
successful post-state renames under the swap.

Registered P-ADDRESS-1 parent. For two nonzero callers, the source-shaped
`run` admits `a₁` iff it admits `a₂` on the caller-swapped input, and a
successful post-state renames under the same swap. The claim is unconditional
over four modeled address-bearing writer projections: since wave 5,
`addressEquivarianceEntryScope` covers `claimWithdrawalsTo` too -- its
request-owner gate (`caller = requestOwner`) is caller-relative and renames
with the caller (`requestOwner` is an address-indexed input field renamed by
`renameInput`) -- so the scope is total over the modeled writers
(`addressEquivarianceEntryScope_total`). The wave-4 scope premise thereby
became vacuous: the source lemmas below hold for every `EntryPoint` via
`run_rename`, so the premise's deletion cannot break the proof, and per the
wave-4 load-bearing criterion it is no longer carried. On
`requestWithdrawals` and `unwrap`, admission is pause plus the caller's own
balance/allowance flags only (`pause_balance_admitted_is_permissionless`); it
does not test `caller = owner` or `caller = <fixed constant>`. Adding a
fixed-owner gate to that admission breaks equivariance via
`LidoSRv3.Tests.AddressSourceMutants.fixed_owner_gate_kill_line_refutes_parent`,
which negates this theorem's exact predicate shape on a mutant of this file's
own `admitted`/`run`/`renameInput` (not an unrelated toy entrypoint).

`wellFormedAddressInput` and `singletonActorEntryPoint` are deliberately not
carried as hypotheses here: neither restricts this conclusion (the proof
below needs only `a₁, a₂ ≠ 0`), and `singletonActorEntryPoint` is provably
`False` for every `EntryPoint` in this model
(`not_singleton_actor_entry_point`), so requiring its negation would add no
content while reading as a real exclusion. Carrying either as an unused
binder would hide that they are premise-free rather than making the claim
more honest. -/
theorems.statement:
theorem universal_address_writer_equivariance
    (a₁ a₂ : Verity.Address) (h₁ : a₁ ≠ 0) (h₂ : a₂ ≠ 0)
    (inp : LidoSRv3.Audit.SolidityAddress.Input) :
    AdmissionIsCallerBlind a₁ a₂ inp ∧ PostStateRenamesWithCaller a₁ a₂ inp

theorems.role: registered Verity Executable Contract parent (audit/guarantees.yaml verity.theorem)
theorems.name: LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PAddress1.abstract_source_verity_tx_address_equivariance
theorems.doc:
/-- Two nonzero callers have the same source-shaped admission bit, and a
successful post-state renames under the swap. Verity composition adds
`Contract.run` observe = `sourceAddressView` when the amount fits one word
and the balance/allowance flags are coherent, snapshot rollback on revert, and
the renamed run observing the renamed view.

Composition of (i) the universal source-shaped swap, (ii) each
`Contract.run` entrypoint's address-write `observe` matching
`sourceAddressView` when `amount < 2^256` and the balance/allowance
flags are coherent, (iii) any `Contract.run` revert restoring the
snapshot, (iv) the renamed input's TX view matching `postAddressView`
of the renamed post-state. Not a WQ claim. -/
theorems.statement:
theorem abstract_source_verity_tx_address_equivariance :
    (∀ (a₁ a₂ : Verity.Address), a₁ ≠ 0 → a₂ ≠ 0 →
      ∀ (inp : LidoSRv3.Audit.SolidityAddress.Input),
      AdmissionIsCallerBlind a₁ a₂ inp) ∧
    (∀ (a₁ a₂ : Verity.Address), a₁ ≠ 0 → a₂ ≠ 0 →
      ∀ (inp : LidoSRv3.Audit.SolidityAddress.Input),
      PostStateRenamesWithCaller a₁ a₂ inp) ∧
    (∀ (inp : LidoSRv3.Audit.SolidityAddress.Input),
      AmountFitsWord inp → BalanceFlagCoherent inp → AllowanceFlagCoherent inp →
      ObservesSourceView inp) ∧
    RevertRestoresSnapshot ∧
    (∀ (a₁ a₂ : Verity.Address), a₁ ≠ 0 → a₂ ≠ 0 →
      ∀ (inp : LidoSRv3.Audit.SolidityAddress.Input) (post : PostState),
      LidoSRv3.Audit.SolidityAddress.run inp = .committed post →
      AmountFitsWord inp → BalanceFlagCoherent inp → AllowanceFlagCoherent inp →
      RenamedRunObservesRenamedView a₁ a₂ inp post)

general rule (Thomas 2026-09-12) applied to P-ADDRESS-1 `externalCallSucceeds` free boolean: new naming scaffold LidoSRv3/Audit/Guarantees/PAddress1BridgeCallPremise.lean introduces `PinnedBridgeCallShape` — a structure that NAMES the pinned Bridge CALL semantics (per-writer `externalCallBindTo` frames in `AddressRecipientCallBridge`, per chantier 6 subordinate P-ADDRESS-1.recipient-call-bridge) as the composition entry point for the `Input.externalCallSucceeds` boolean. **Status: naming scaffold, not a full composition** — the `externalCallSucceeds_derived_under_pinned_bridge_shape` theorem is a straight-line projection. A real derivation requires per-writer Bridge-to-source glue lemmas connecting `Bridge.callee (ctx) (world) = .success ...` to `inputs.externalCallSucceeds = true`. That glue is not tree-resident yet; the Bridge module proves caller-and-callee-world rollback but does not export per-writer `externalCallSucceeds` derivations. Downstream consumers can supply a `PinnedBridgeCallShape` bundle once the glue is proved.

**real-derivation first step for externalCallSucceeds** (2026-09-13, following general rule): new source module LidoSRv3/Audit/Source/BridgeCallResultSource.lean defines `BridgeCallOutcome { succeeded : Bool }` and `externalCallSucceedsFromBridge outcome = outcome.succeeded` — a source-level function of the Bridge callee's success bit. New composition `externalCallSucceeds_derived_from_bridge_outcome` in `PAddress1BridgeCallPremise` derives `inp.externalCallSucceeds = true` from an `ExternalCallFromBridge inp outcome` linkage premise + `outcome.succeeded = true` via `externalCallSucceeds_true_of_bridge_succeeded`. Real derivation, not a projection. Composition value: the `externalCallSucceeds` entry now goes through a named `BridgeCallOutcome` source read instead of an anonymous free `Bool`. Residual: `BridgeCallOutcome.succeeded` is still an input boolean; per-writer Bridge-to-source glue (connecting the actual `externalCallBindTo` frame per callee to the source outcome) remains the next follow-up.

**per-writer Bridge-to-source glue second step** (2026-09-13, following general rule): new source module LidoSRv3/Audit/Source/BridgePerWriterGlue.lean defines a `Writer` inductive (requestWithdrawals / claimWithdrawals / unwrap / transferFrom) and four per-writer BridgeCallOutcome constructors, each identifying the pinned Solidity callee: `bridgeOutcomeForRequestWithdrawals` names `STETH.transferFrom` at WithdrawalQueue.sol:374; `bridgeOutcomeForClaimWithdrawals` names value CALL at WithdrawalQueueBase.sol:472; `bridgeOutcomeForUnwrap` names `stETH.transfer` at WstETH.sol:73; `bridgeOutcomeForTransferFrom` names the non-callable path at WithdrawalQueueERC721.sol:248 (trivially succeeded). Dispatcher `bridgeOutcomeForWriter` selects per-writer. `bridgeOutcomeForWriter_succeeded` proves the dispatcher's success bit for each writer definitionally. Composition value: the composition entry now identifies WHICH pinned callee is being read, not just an anonymous bridge outcome. Residual: live-callee execution model (per-writer Bridge executable-plane connection) remains follow-up.

chantier 6 guard-order inversion #1 (mandate 2026-09-12): the Verity `AddressTx` model of `WithdrawalQueue.transferFrom` (`LidoSRv3/Audit/Verity/AddressTx.lean:82-88`) checks `balance >= amount` (line 84, `InsufficientBalance`) BEFORE `allowance >= amount` (line 86, `InsufficientAllowance`). The pinned Solidity source at `contracts/0.4.24/StETH.sol` for the analogous StETH `transferFrom` inverts this: allowance is decremented (via `_spendAllowance`) BEFORE the balance-debit `_transfer` in the ERC-20 flow. Two failure modes with the same account state therefore surface with different revert reasons on the two planes (Verity model reports `InsufficientBalance` where pinned StETH would report `InsufficientAllowance`). The registered parent's success/rollback conjuncts are ADDRESS-EQUIVARIANT over the model's own admission function and are not sensitive to which revert reason fires; the guard-order divergence is therefore invisible to the parent but a real fidelity gap of the modelled `transferFrom` correspondence.

chantier 6 guard-order inversion #2 (mandate 2026-09-12): the Verity `AddressTx` model of `WithdrawalQueue._claim` (`AddressTx.lean:109-111`) checks `hintValid` (line 109, `InvalidHint`) BEFORE the request-owner gate `ownerWord == addressToWord sender` (line 111, `NotRequestOwner`). The pinned Solidity `WithdrawalQueue.claimWithdrawalsTo` sequence (contracts/0.8.9/WithdrawalQueue.sol) enforces the owner-or-approved check FIRST in `claimWithdrawalsTo` before calling `_claim`, which then runs `_checkHint`. So the pinned Solidity's owner-then-hint ordering is INVERTED to hint-then-owner in the Verity model. A malformed hint on a not-yet-owned request therefore reverts `InvalidHint` on the Verity plane but `NotOwnerOrApproved` on the pinned Solidity. The registered parent's address-equivariance is not sensitive to the revert-reason ordering, but the `AddressClaimBatchTx` per-request receipt shape is; this remains a fidelity gap of the modelled `_claim` sequence.

chantier 6 parent shape disclosure (mandate 2026-09-12): the registered abstract parent `universal_address_writer_equivariance` is a BOOLEAN-PROJECTION theorem on `SolidityAddress.admitted` / `run` with a caller-relative renaming, and does NOT track any state indexed by address (the `AddressState` record models a scoped subset of the pinned storage; the parent's `run` produces a committed post-state that is renamed by `renameInput`/`renameOutput` but not indexed by address in the sense of an address→word mapping keyed by callers). Address-indexed storage — balances, allowances, per-address request lists — remains a separate model plane (`AddressClaimBatchTx` uses `mapUint` channels for the claim-loop, but the parent's success shape is projection-level, not physical-mapping-level).

chantier 6 (mandate 2026-09-12): the `LidoSRv3/Audit/Verity/AddressRecipientCallBridge.lean` module carries the real CALL evidence for the four permissionless writers — the executable `externalCallBindTo`-based call frames for `claimWithdrawalsTo` (`claim_withdrawals_to_revert_restores_caller_and_callee_world`), `unwrap` (`unwrap_bridge_receipt`, `unwrap_revert_restores_caller_and_callee_world`), `transferFrom` (`transfer_revert_restores_world`), and `requestWithdrawals` (`request_revert_restores_caller_and_callee_world`), plus the caller-and-callee-world rollback (`revert_restores_caller_and_callee_world`) and the EOA-recipient empty-value receipt (`eoa_empty_value_call_receipt`). These bridge theorems are NOT folded into the registered Verity parent `abstract_source_verity_tx_address_equivariance`; the parent still consumes address-writer observables via the projection plane and does not compose with the bridge's caller-and-callee-world rollback. Registered as subordinate `P-ADDRESS-1.recipient-call-bridge`.

chantier 6 report correction (mandate 2026-09-12): `report/P-ADDRESS-1.md` previously cited `PAddress1.bounded_live_claim_batch_storage_call_surface`, a theorem that does not exist in `LidoSRv3/`. Corrected to name the actual live-batch evidence: `LidoSRv3.Audit.Model.AddressClaimJournalLegacy.two_claim_batch_observe` (two-item receipt) and `LidoSRv3.Audit.Verity.AddressClaimBatchTx.every_revert_restores_snapshot` (universal failed-run rollback).

general-rule residual (Thomas 2026-09-12, updated 2026-09-13 after real-derivation first step): `externalCallSucceeds` composition now routes through the source-level function `externalCallSucceedsFromBridge` on a named `BridgeCallOutcome` — a real derivation step. Remaining follow-up: per-writer glue lemmas connecting the actual `externalCallBindTo` frame per callee (requestWithdrawals, unwrap, claimWithdrawalsTo, transferFrom) to the source `BridgeCallOutcome.succeeded` field. Once those glue lemmas land, `BridgeCallOutcome` becomes a function of the actual Bridge callee execution.

model_not_deployment: These are proofs about a model, not about a deployed contract.
The subject is a Lean model of Staking Router v3, written against pinned source lidofinance/core@17005714f151e5502c559932319a3f2f74ac2436.

No theorem here binds to deployed bytecode, a runtime codehash, a constructor, or a chain address. The SRv3 contracts are deployed on mainnet with lidofinance/core v4.0.0 (2026-07-24; StakingRouter proxy 0xFdDf38947aFB03C621C71b06C9C70bce73f12999, TopUpGateway proxy 0x3FC2C71579D80790Aaa3fc7Be8B66ac39dC57374); the theorems still speak about the model, not about that deployment.
CHECKED means *the named Lean theorem builds*. It does not mean audited, verified on chain, or closed.
Every row below still has open fidelity gaps — 105 in total. The last column counts them per row; audit/guarantees.yaml names each one.
